definitions.gloss: standard language; common speech; everyday language
definitions.explanation: The form of a language used in general communication, as opposed to dialect, technical jargon, or literary language. In the Japanese context, refers to the common spoken language as distinct from regional dialects.

examples.japanese: {普通語|ふつうご}で{話|はな}してください。
{方言|ほうげん}ではなく{普通語|ふつうご}で{書|か}かれた{文章|ぶんしょう}だ。
examples.english: This is a text written in standard language, not dialect.

examples.japanese: {専門|せんもん}{用語|ようご}を{避|さ}けて{普通語|ふつうご}で{説明|せつめい}するよう{心|こころ}がけている。
examples.english: I try to explain things in everyday language, avoiding technical terms.

notes:
A compound of {普通|ふつう} (ordinary; common) and {語|ご} (language; word). Can refer to either the standard/common form of a language (as opposed to dialects) or to everyday vocabulary (as opposed to jargon). In Chinese linguistics, {普通語|ふつうご} specifically refers to Mandarin Chinese (Putonghua), and this usage also appears in Japanese texts about Chinese language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {普通語|ふつうご}で{話|はな}す: to speak in standard language
- {普通語|ふつうご}に{直|なお}す: to convert to standard language
- {普通語|ふつうご}と{方言|ほうげん}: standard language and dialect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {標準語|ひょうじゅんご}: standard language — the officially designated national standard, more formal term
- {共通語|きょうつうご}: common language — language understood across regions; emphasizes mutual intelligibility
- {口語|こうご}: spoken language; colloquial language — contrasts with written or literary language
